chapter.name: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
chapter.blurb: Growth and the stages of life, adolescence and puberty, the menstrual cycle, emotional changes, nutrition and hygiene, physical activity and social media, and avoiding harmful substances.

concepts.name: Growth, stages of life and adolescence
concepts.description: Growth of plants and animals, the stages of human life, and the visible physical changes of adolescence.
concepts.idea: Adolescence is a stage between childhood and adulthood, from about 10 to 19 years, with rapid growth.
concepts.rule: A plant grows from a seed to a sapling and then matures to produce flowers, fruits and seeds; similarly animals must grow and mature before they can reproduce. Human life has stages: infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age, and each person goes through them at their own pace. Until about 10-12 years most changes are in height and weight; then adolescence begins, a period of rapid growth typically between the ages of 10 and 19, when the body prepares for adulthood. Visible changes include increase in height, weight, strength, broader shoulders and wider chest in boys and development of breasts in girls. In boys the voice box grows, giving a hoarse voice and sometimes an Adam's apple; girls have only slight voice change. Acne (pimples) occurs due to increased oily secretions clogging skin pores. Hair grows in the armpits and pubic region in both, and facial hair in boys. The timing and extent of these changes vary and are normal.
concepts.example: Venkatesh's voice changed and he developed a thin moustache, while Devyani grew taller.

concepts.name: Puberty, secondary sexual characteristics and the menstrual cycle
concepts.description: Secondary sexual characteristics, puberty, the menstrual cycle and myths about menstruation.
concepts.idea: Puberty prepares the body for reproduction, and menstruation is a natural process.
concepts.rule: Some characteristic changes, such as change in voice, facial and chest hair in boys and development of breasts in girls, are not directly involved in reproduction but help distinguish males from females. These are secondary sexual characteristics and are natural signs that the body is preparing for adulthood, marking the onset of puberty. Puberty is the stage when the body of an adolescent undergoes external and internal changes to become an adult capable of reproduction. Internal changes include maturation of the parts involved in reproduction. In girls the menstrual cycle begins; it recurs generally every 28-30 days (healthy cycles may range from 21 to 35 days) and blood discharge, called menstruation, lasts three to seven days. Some girls may feel pain or discomfort. Menstruation stops naturally by age 45-55. Myths and taboos about menstruation, such as isolating girls, have no scientific basis.
concepts.example: The menstrual cycle is one of the signs of good reproductive health.

concepts.name: Emotional and behavioural changes in adolescents
concepts.description: Mood swings, stronger emotions and sensitivity, their effects on behaviour and ways to grow positively.
concepts.idea: Adolescence brings stronger emotions, and positive activities help manage them.
concepts.rule: Adolescence is marked by emotional and behavioural changes as well as physical ones. Key emotional changes include mood swings, strong emotions and increased sensitivity. Their probable effects on behaviour include quick changes of feeling, deeper interest in new areas, or joining social initiatives to support the needy and disadvantaged. Ways for positive growth include engaging in varied activities like music, dance or sports, self-exploration and involvement in creative activities and innovation, and compassion and social work. Understanding how our emotions influence our behaviour helps us make better choices and respond to situations thoughtfully.

concepts.name: Nutrition and personal hygiene, including menstrual hygiene
concepts.description: The need for a balanced diet, nutrients and their sources, iron and vitamin B12, and hygiene with government schemes.
concepts.idea: A balanced diet and hygiene keep adolescents healthy, and government schemes support menstrual health.
concepts.rule: Adolescence is a period of growth so a nutritious diet is very important: proteins and carbohydrates for growth and energy, and enough fats, vitamins and minerals. Milk, millets, curd, cheese and paneer give calcium, proteins and fats, with calcium helping bone growth. Spinach, kidney beans, raisins and figs give iron, which helps in the formation of blood. Adolescents, especially girls, may suffer from blood-related problems due to iron or vitamin B12 deficiency. Dorothy Hodgkin studied vitamin B12 and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1964. Personal hygiene, particularly of armpits and pubic region, prevents infections. During menstruation hygiene can be maintained with sanitary pads or reusable cloth pads; used pads should be wrapped in newspaper and put in a dustbin, and biodegradable pads are available. Schemes include the Menstrual Hygiene Scheme, Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram, Suvidha Sanitary Napkin Initiative and state schemes like Shuchi in Karnataka.

concepts.name: Physical activity, social life and cyberbullying
concepts.description: Exercise and fitness, polite social behaviour, responsible use of social media, and cyberbullying.
concepts.idea: Exercise and responsible behaviour, offline and online, support a healthy adolescence.
concepts.rule: Regular exercise and physical activities keep body and mind fit and healthy, build stamina and boost mood. Adolescents should be polite and respectful and thoughtful and responsible when interacting in person or through social media. They may feel attracted to peers and mimic their behaviour, and interact online. Online platforms give information and connections and should be used responsibly for collective well-being; seeking guidance from elders and teachers helps. Cyberbullying is using digital devices to harass others by sending misleading messages, spreading false rumours or sharing personal information without consent. If someone bullies you, do not feel scared or helpless; handle it wisely and seek help from parents and teachers. Be cautious about uploading pictures or sharing personal information with strangers. Social media dos: be respectful and kind, think before posting, protect privacy.
concepts.example: Do not share personal photos with strangers or virtual friends.

concepts.name: Harmful substances, hormones and asking 'why'
concepts.description: Substance abuse and saying no, help and government initiatives, and hormones as the cause of adolescent changes.
concepts.idea: Harmful substances damage health and are addictive, and hormones control the changes of adolescence.
concepts.rule: Some people or peers may pressure adolescents to consume harmful substances such as tobacco, gutka, cigarettes, beedi, alcohol or illegal drugs. These are harmful to physical and mental health and are addictive: once started, a strong urge to take them again and again develops, leading to regular use called substance abuse. They cause breathing difficulties, memory loss and lung damage. The advice is to say NO the first time and every time and to stay firm and confident. Seek help from family, friends, parents or teachers, and counselling and medical advice can help. The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment spreads awareness, especially among early-age children, and the National De-addiction Helpline is 14446. Many adolescent changes, including menstruation, are mainly due to hormones, chemicals produced in the body that regulate growth and development, released in response to signals from the brain; some influence mood and behaviour.
concepts.example: Someone addicted today might have started once with 'just one time'.
